note: Host runtime registry for Super Loop. PURE DATA: maps a host runtime (the agent the operator is driving) to its continuous-mode driver, driver family, MCP config paths, and integration tier. Extensible — add a host by adding an entry here, no code change. This is DISTINCT from KNOWN_ROUTE_CLIS in host.mjs (which is about which worker CLIs are installed on PATH). 'verified' marks whether the slash command/behavior was confirmed against a primary source; an unverified entry links its docs and must NOT be presented as certain. NOTE: claude-code / codex / unknown engageStep + command are intentionally mirrored from constants.CONTINUOUS_MODE_BY_HOST during the gradual migration; hostregistry.test.mjs locks the commands together so they cannot drift. engine.buildHostSetup() consolidates onto this registry in a later step.

tiers.1: Native goal: the host has a progress-driven continuous command (e.g. /goal). Engage it with an operator-stop objective.
tiers.2: MCP + continuation contract: no reliable continuous slash command — drive it with a host rules snippet (call recommendedNextAction every turn; checkpoint != stop).
tiers.3: CLI owns the loop: drive the whole campaign with the super-loop-run CLI (the universal fallback) instead of host turns.

goal_progress.mechanism: next turn starts when the previous finishes; an evaluator checks a completion condition
goal_progress.superLoopFit: best — engage the goal with an operator-stop objective

loop_interval.mechanism: wake on a fixed timer (poll every N minutes)
loop_interval.superLoopFit: wrong default for Super Loop (polling, not convergence)

loop_self_pace.mechanism: turn ends, the model schedules its own wake-up
loop_self_pace.superLoopFit: works but chunky for a long MCP campaign; prefer goal_progress

plugin_goal.mechanism: goal-style convergence via an installed plugin
plugin_goal.superLoopFit: tier 1 once the plugin is installed; document the requirement

mcp_reactive.mechanism: no continuous slash command; the host only re-enters when prompted
mcp_reactive.superLoopFit: tier 2 — ship a rules snippet: continue on every tool result, checkpoint != stop

auto_continue.mechanism: config/hooks inject 'keep going' or a heartbeat/cron re-enters
auto_continue.superLoopFit: tier 2 — standing order + autoContinue, or spawn a goal-progress child agent

orchestrator.mechanism: a multi-agent mission layer drives worker sessions
orchestrator.superLoopFit: Super Loop is a measured tool INSIDE a mission worker, not the orchestrator

internal_loop.mechanism: the agent runs its own while-loop until max steps / idle
internal_loop.superLoopFit: call Super Loop tools each turn inside the host loop, or use the CLI fallback

cli_autonomous.mechanism: the super-loop-run package drives workers itself
cli_autonomous.superLoopFit: universal fallback — works on any host with no good continuous primitive

unknown.superLoopFit: set SUPER_LOOP_HOST, or use the super-loop-run CLI fallback

primaryDriver.note: progress-driven: the next turn starts automatically when the previous finishes; a fast model checks the completion condition

alternateDrivers.note: interval polling (e.g. /loop 5m) — wrong default for a convergence campaign
self-paced wake-ups (1m-1h) — chunky for a long MCP campaign; prefer /goal

hosts.engageStep: Engage continuous mode now: run /goal with this objective: "{OBJECTIVE}", and give it a completion condition only the operator can satisfy — Claude Code starts the next turn automatically when the previous finishes and keeps driving until the operator stops you. Never let the goal complete on a measurement checkpoint (EXEC_DISABLED / saturation / no-improvement) — those are not stops. (/loop is for interval polling or self-paced wake-ups, not this convergence campaign.)
hosts.goalConditionTemplate: Super Loop run {runId} stays ACTIVE: keep calling Super Loop tools every turn; the operator is the only stop — not saturation, EXEC_DISABLED, or dashboard checkpoints.

primaryDriver.note: create a Codex goal and keep it active across turns

hosts.engageStep: Engage continuous mode now: create a Codex goal (/goal) with this objective: "{OBJECTIVE}", and keep it active across turns. Never mark the goal blocked or complete on a measurement checkpoint (EXEC_DISABLED / saturation / no-improvement) — those are not stops.
hosts.goalConditionTemplate: Super Loop run {runId} stays ACTIVE: keep calling Super Loop tools every turn; the operator is the only stop.

primaryDriver.note: modeled on Codex /goal (pause/replace/clear) — CONFIRM against ZCode docs before relying on it

hosts.engageStep: Engage continuous mode now: create a /goal with this objective: "{OBJECTIVE}" and keep it active across turns (ZCode's goal driver is reported to mirror Codex; confirm the exact command in your build). Never complete the goal on a measurement checkpoint (EXEC_DISABLED / saturation / no-improvement). If ZCode has no /goal in your build, fall back to the super-loop-run CLI.
hosts.goalConditionTemplate: Super Loop run {runId} stays ACTIVE: keep calling Super Loop tools every turn; the operator is the only stop.

primaryDriver.note: REQUIRES a goal plugin — OpenCode has no native goal driver

requires: an OpenCode goal plugin (e.g. opencode-goal); without it OpenCode is mcp_reactive (tier 2)
hosts.engageStep: Install/enable an OpenCode goal plugin, then engage /goal with this objective: "{OBJECTIVE}" and keep it active. If no goal plugin is installed, treat OpenCode as tier 2 (drive it with the continuation rules snippet) or use the super-loop-run CLI fallback.
hosts.goalConditionTemplate: Super Loop run {runId} stays ACTIVE: keep calling Super Loop tools every turn; the operator is the only stop.

primaryDriver.note: no continuous slash command — drive via a host rules snippet

hosts.engageStep: Cursor has no continuous goal command. Add the Super Loop continuation rule to your project rules (.cursor/rules): after every Super Loop tool result with campaignContinues:true, immediately call recommendedNextAction; never end the turn on 'converged' while runStatus is ACTIVE; checkpoints are not stops. For a hands-off run, use the super-loop-run CLI.

primaryDriver.note: IDE modes have no continuous slash command; the CLI is an OpenCode fork (tier 1 only with a goal plugin)

hosts.engageStep: Kilo Code (IDE) has no continuous goal command — drive it with the Super Loop continuation rules snippet (continue on every tool result; checkpoint != stop). The Kilo CLI is an OpenCode fork, so a goal plugin promotes it to tier 1; otherwise use the super-loop-run CLI fallback.

primaryDriver.note: config/heartbeat re-entry, not a slash command

hosts.engageStep: OpenClaw keeps going via config (autoContinue / heartbeat / cron), not a slash command. Set a standing order to call recommendedNextAction every turn and enable autoContinue; or spawn a goal-progress child agent (Codex/Claude via ACP) and run the campaign under it. Checkpoints are not stops. The super-loop-run CLI is the no-babysitting fallback.

primaryDriver.note: runs its own ReAct/cron loop — call Super Loop tools each turn inside it

hosts.engageStep: Hermes already runs its own internal loop. Call the Super Loop tools each turn inside that loop (it is the measured referee, not the driver); for coding work it can delegate to a Claude/Codex child. For batch/headless runs, use the super-loop-run CLI fallback.

primaryDriver.note: Missions orchestrate worker sessions; Super Loop runs as a tool INSIDE a mission worker, not as the orchestrator

hosts.engageStep: Don't fight the Missions orchestrator. Run Super Loop INSIDE a mission worker: mission objective 'Harden loop X with Super Loop', and the worker session calls initialize_loop_run -> loop-de-loop -> the gates. For headless runs, droid exec can drive the super-loop-run CLI.

primaryDriver.note: runs a max_steps agent loop — call Super Loop tools inside it, or drive via the CLI

hosts.engageStep: MiniMax Mini-Agent runs a max_steps agent loop. Call the Super Loop tools inside that loop each step, or drive the whole campaign with the super-loop-run CLI fallback.

primaryDriver.note: host not identified — set SUPER_LOOP_HOST, or drive the campaign with the super-loop-run CLI fallback

hosts.engageStep: Engage your runtime’s native continuous/agentic mode now with this objective: "{OBJECTIVE}". Claude Code → /goal (progress-driven; /loop only for interval polling or self-paced wake-ups); Codex → /goal; other runtimes → your equivalent continuous loop command. Keep it active until the operator stops you.
